records.name: Slow Food Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Slow Food movement. It runs social and learning dinners and gives a Snail of Approval award to local food businesses that meet its standards for good, clean, and fair food.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a chapter dinner or workshop, or join as a member for $60 a year to get discounts on some events and early notice of new ones. Volunteers can help through partner programs, such as Sunday Suppers, Greensgrow Farm (which asks new volunteers to attend an orientation first), or a hoop house project that grows food for seniors' meals.

schedule.text: Dinners, tastings, cooking workshops and book groups are posted on the events page as they are planned, so check there for the next one.

locations.label: Queen Village (address not on the event listing)

cost.text: Membership is $60 a year and includes discounts on select events. Event tickets are set one event at a time, and recent listings range from free to $95.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket from an event listing, or join as a member for $60 a year through the join page. Questions go through the contact form on the Contact Us page, since no email address is published.
first_step.basis: Events are public and ticketed, and the join page is open to anyone. The site does not say that beginners are specifically welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Chapter dinners are social evenings for members and friends, with a set menu and a limited number of seats. The banquet listing says the meal is gluten free, that guests bring their own drinks, and that allergies cannot be accommodated. The listing does not say how the meal is served, so ask the chapter before you buy if that matters to you.
first_visit_tips: If a listing says BYOB, bring your own drinks.
Tell the chapter about any food allergy before you buy, because the banquet listing says allergies cannot be accommodated.
The event listing does not give the venue address, so ask through the contact form before the night.

records.notes: The home page text says 'There are currently no events scheduled' in one place, which conflicts with the October 22, 2026 banquet on the events page; the banquet listing was used. The banquet listing shows both $30 and 'Total Price: Free'; the $30 ticket price is used. Past event listings show no year, so they were not used as dated evidence. The volunteer page names partner programs (Sunday Suppers, Greensgrow Farm, Klein JCC Grow for a Friend, Community Partnership School, Vetri Community Partnership, Agatston Urban Nutrition Initiative); these are in leads_only and were not fetched in this run. Venue address, dress code, accessibility and languages are not on any page read, so they are left out.

records.name: Smith Memorial Playground & Playhouse
records.summary: A free play space in East Fairmount Park with a giant wooden slide, an indoor playhouse, and a nature play area. Volunteers have helped with planting, weeding, mulching, story time, crafts, and the yearly appeal mailing.
records.what_you_do: Help with grounds work, support story time or crafts for families, or help with the yearly appeal mailing. You can also suggest a volunteer project to staff.

schedule.text: Closed Mondays. April to September: Tuesday to Friday 10 am to 6 pm, Saturday and Sunday 10 am to 7 pm. October to March: Tuesday to Sunday 10 am to 5 pm. The playground closes at dusk in fall and winter, and hours depend on the weather. The site sometimes closes for private events or maintenance, so check the website before you go.

cost.text: Daily visits are free. Group visits cost $25 for 11 to 25 children, $50 for 26 to 50, $75 for 51 to 75, and $100 for 76 to 100. Groups of 10 or more children need an advance reservation, and group visits run on weekdays, 10 am to 12 pm or 1 pm to 3 pm.

access.notes: Service animals are welcome under ADA guidelines, but other animals are not allowed. Bus 32 stops at 33rd and Oxford Streets, then about a third of a mile on foot. Bus 3 stops at 33rd and Cecil B. Moore Streets, then one block south and about a third of a mile on foot; on weekends during visiting hours it runs directly to Smith.

first_step.how: Visit during open hours, with no sign up needed for a daily visit. To volunteer, email Jim Neal, Director of Facilities & Operations, at jim@smithplayground.org or call 215.765.4325 extension 101, since he takes all volunteer questions.
first_step.basis: Daily visits are free and open to the public, and volunteer questions go to one named staff contact. The site does not describe a newcomer program or a first-visit routine.
first_step.what_to_expect: A daily visit is free and is made for children, and children must always be with an adult. The playground covers about six and a half acres with climbing, swinging and spinning zones, and the Playhouse has three floors of interactive play. Groups of 10 or more children need to book ahead.
first_visit_tips: Check the hours first: the site is closed on Mondays, and the playground closes at dusk in fall and winter.
Park in the free lot in front of the Playhouse, or on Reservoir Drive when the lot is full, and do not leave valuables in the car.
Bring your own food if you want it, since options within walking distance are very limited. Grilling and BBQing are not allowed.
The site is designed mainly for children 10 and under, and a grown-up must supervise every child.

records.notes: Hours and admission match on the home page and the plan-your-visit page. The Things to Do page has no accessibility, stroller, elevator or quiet-hour detail, so it is not cited. Wheelchair, stroller and elevator access are not stated on any page read, so no wheelchair value is recorded. The Rules and Safety section is linked from the plan page but was not read. The volunteer page links to a document of current volunteer needs, which was not read.

records.name: Society for Creative Anachronism
records.summary: Penn's student chapter of a volunteer group that recreates crafts, music, dance and combat from before the 1600s. Members practice these skills and show them at events and demonstrations.
records.what_you_do: Members meet for period dance practice, craft nights and workshops. Guests without a PennCard must email the chatelaine at least 24 hours before a practice to be added to a name list, and the name must match the photo ID shown at the door.

schedule.text: A European dance practice aims to meet every other Monday from 7 to 9 pm in a campus library room. Some sessions run 7:30 to 9:30 pm instead. Craft nights, demonstrations and Arts and Sciences hangouts are listed on the chapter's event pages.

locations.label: Van Pelt Library, Class of '55 Room (Room 241), 2nd floor, University of Pennsylvania
Fisher Fine Arts Library, Davis Seminar Room, University of Pennsylvania

access.notes: The dance practice room is on the 2nd floor of Van Pelt Library, reached by elevator.

first_step.how: Email the chatelaine at chatelaine@ivyeinrust.eastkingdom.org at least 24 hours before a practice so your name goes on the list, then come to the European dance practice. Guests who have a PennCard do not need the list.
first_step.basis: The chapter's page says the chatelaine welcomes newcomers and is their first contact. The dance page does not say whether beginners are welcome, so this rating rests on the newcomer note.
first_step.what_to_expect: Practices run about two hours in a campus library room, where a teacher leads 15th and 16th century European dances with live musicians. Anyone without a PennCard must be on the name list, and the name must match the photo ID shown at the door. The chapter does not publish a cost or a dress code, so ask the chatelaine before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Bring a photo ID that matches the name you sent to the chatelaine.
Enter Van Pelt Library, take the elevators to the 2nd floor, and follow the hallway to the room just before the arched entry to Lippincott Library.
Send your email at least 24 hours before the practice.

records.notes: Tier 1 said guests should RSVP the Friday before. The chapter's own dance page says to email the chatelaine at least 24 hours before practice, and that rule is used here. The chatelaine's Get Started page was not read: the guessed URL returned 404, and the home page links to officers pages instead. The Upcoming Events page says no events are in planning, which conflicts with dated 2026 events on the home page and the Arts and Sciences page (October 5, October 12, October 19 and October 26, 2026); the dated pages are used. The Arts and Sciences page's name list note refers to the dance practice, which looks like a copy error, so confirm the deadline with the chatelaine. Cost, dress code and beginner policy are not stated on the pages read.

records.name: Society Hill Synagogue
records.summary: A congregation at 418 Spruce Street in Society Hill with Friday evening and Saturday morning services, a weekly Monday evening minyan on Zoom, a playschool for children ages 18 months to 5, and a Hebrew school.
records.what_you_do: Join Friday evening or Saturday morning Shabbat services and the meals after them, take an adult education course (the Nuts and Bolts introduction to Judaism is written for people new to the faith), enroll a child in the playschool or Hebrew school, or join the Monday evening minyan on Zoom. Membership and renewals are handled through an online form.

schedule.text: Shabbat services are held on Friday evenings and Saturday mornings in the sanctuary, and a Monday evening minyan meets on Zoom. Meals follow Shabbat and holiday services. The site does not print service times, and adult education runs as multi-week courses through the year.

cost.text: Membership dues and school tuition are paid through an online link on the site, and the amounts are not listed. Adult education courses have a member price and a general public price, such as $18 for members and $108 for the public on a nine-session course.

access.notes: Wheelchair users can enter through the Paula Kline Learning Center door on Spruce Street. An elevator serves the first and second floors and the rear courtyard. Accessibility requests go to Executive Director Sahar Oz at soz@societyhillsynagogue.org or 215-922-6590 extension 3.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-922-6590 Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, or join through the membership form on the site. For a first class, register for the Nuts and Bolts course, which is written for people new to Judaism and those coming back to it.
first_step.basis: The site has a beginner course for people new to Judaism, says all are welcome, and tells visitors to call or use the membership form. It does not describe a formal guest or first-visit policy, so it stops short of a top rating.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shabbat services are held in the sanctuary on Friday evenings and Saturday mornings, and the Saturday service includes a discussion of the week's Torah portion. Adult courses run for several sessions, mostly in person, with a Zoom option on some. The site does not describe a guest policy or dress code, so ask the office what a first visit looks like.
first_visit_tips: Free street parking for Friday evening and Saturday morning services is on west 5th Street (Lombard to Walnut) and east 6th Street (Spruce to Pine). Those spots are No Stopping lanes, so pick up the parking placard in the lobby first.
Register ahead for an adult course, which the site recommends. Zoom links and passcodes go to registrants.
If you use a wheelchair, enter through the Paula Kline Learning Center door on Spruce Street, and use the elevator to reach the first or second floor.

records.notes: Service times are not printed on the site, so only the days and general times are recorded. The Join Us, Shabbat, Minyan, Playschool and Hebrew School pages were linked from the home page but could not be read: the guessed URLs returned 404 and the fetch budget was spent on the others. Playschool age range comes from the home page. Dues amounts are not listed on any page read. Bus routes 12 and 57 are named on the directions page without stop names, so no nearest stop is recorded. The calendar page was not read. The Pay Dues link goes to a third-party payment page and is not cited as a contact.

records.name: Somerton United Methodist Church
records.summary: A United Methodist church on Bustleton Avenue with a weekly Tuesday food bank, a volunteer choir that welcomes new singers, and space for community recovery groups.
records.what_you_do: Drop off non-perishable food at the church before or after services. To volunteer at the food bank or ask about getting help, use the Somerton Foodbank website, which the church names. You can also join the volunteer choir, which has no auditions, or ask the church office about groups and ministries.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:45 am, with children taking part in the regular service. Food distribution runs every Tuesday from 10 am to 1 pm. The choir sings during worship and at events, and the church office can tell you about rehearsals. Recovery groups meet in the church building on their own schedules.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:45 am, or call the church office at 215-673-2745 to ask about joining the choir.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are warmly invited whether they are lifelong Methodists or new to faith, and the choir needs no audition and takes singers of any experience. The church office is named as the place to ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:45 am, and children stay in the regular service with some moments made just for them. The pages read do not describe what happens after the service or a first-visit routine. The church office is the best place to ask about the choir, volunteering or recovery groups.
first_visit_tips: Bring a non-perishable food donation if you want, and drop it off before or after the service.
From I-95 south, the directions end with about 2 miles south on Bustleton Avenue, with the church on your right.
For a choir visit, call the office first, since rehearsal days and times are not published on the site.

records.notes: The church site links no separate choir, food ministry, recovery or new-visitor page; the guessed /choir/ URL returned 404, so choir rehearsal times are not recorded. Recovery group meeting times are not on the church site. The contact page shows no phone or email, so the phone number is carried from tier 1 (EPA UMC food ministry map) and is not confirmed on the church site. Office hours and parking are not stated. The Somerton Foodbank website is in leads_only and was not fetched in this run.

records.name: Somos Society
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that collects and shares the stories of the city's Puerto Rican community through films and recorded conversations. Anyone can watch, listen, or add a story of their own.
records.what_you_do: Watch its documentary films, listen to the Domino Dialogues podcast, or share a personal story for the community collection. Groups can also request a screening of one of its documentaries.

schedule.text: The site does not publish a regular schedule. New films, podcast conversations and archive stories are added as they are ready.

cost.text: The site does not mention a fee for watching films, listening to the podcast or sharing a story. Story contributors receive no payment.

first_step.how: Watch a film or listen to the Domino Dialogues podcast, or share a story through the La Historia Colectiva form, which asks for a written memory and an optional photo or video. Questions go to info@somossociety.org.
first_step.basis: The films, podcast and archive are open to the public, and the site gives two clear ways to take part. It does not describe a newcomer program or a first-visit routine.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is mostly online: you can watch the films, listen to the Domino Dialogues podcast, and browse the archive. To take part, you can submit a story, which the team reviews before it is posted, or open the Join the Conversation page. The site does not list office hours, so email first if you plan to stop by.
first_visit_tips: Read the release terms before you send a story: the team may edit it, and your name may be published unless you ask to stay anonymous.
Use the newsletter sign-up on the home page to hear about new films and conversations.

records.notes: The screening events page reads 'Coming Soon' and lists no screenings, so no screening dates or venues are recorded. Tier 1 said the site lists screening events; that is corrected here. The Domino Dialogues podcast page and the Join the Conversation page could not be read: the guessed URLs returned 404, and the homepage links (/the-domino-dialogues-podcast and /domino-dialogues-interest) were not fetched because the budget was spent. Spanish is not mentioned on the story page, so no language codes are recorded. The story page also publishes somossocietydoc@gmail.com for help with submitting; it is noted here and not in contacts. No dated 2026 evidence was found, so status stays probably active.

records.name: South Philadelphia Shtiebel
records.summary: A Jewish community in South Philadelphia for prayer, learning and friendship. The site lists a Zoom room for prayer and study, a Slack group for members, and a kiddush sponsorship for family milestones.
records.what_you_do: Visit in person at 1311 S. Juniper Street, join prayer and learning in the building or on the Zoom room, take part in the Slack community, volunteer with a team, or sponsor a kiddush after a life milestone.

schedule.text: Prayer and study times change through the year and around holidays, so check the site calendar or email before you come. The Zoom room is the online space for learning, prayer and connection.

locations.label: Shtiebel (main space on the second floor)

cost.text: The site does not list membership dues or class fees. It has a donation page and a kiddush sponsorship option.

access.notes: The main space is on the second floor, reached by about 14 stairs, and a chair lift is available for anyone who needs it.

first_step.how: Email info@southphiladelphiashtiebel.org before you visit with any questions, or ask to be connected with a community guide. To join online, use the Zoom room link on the site.
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes people of all backgrounds and invites visitors to ask questions before a visit, and it offers a guide to talk with. It does not describe a formal first-visit or guest routine.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site invites visitors to write in before coming, and it can connect you with a community guide to talk about life at the Shtiebel. The main room is upstairs, reached by stairs or a chair lift. The pages read do not describe the service, dress code or any guest cost, so ask those questions by email first.
first_visit_tips: Email info@southphiladelphiashtiebel.org ahead of time with questions about the neighborhood or about a Shabbat visit.
The main space is upstairs, so ask about the chair lift when you arrive if you need it.
To join the Slack community, email info+slack@southphiladelphiashtiebel.org with the subject line Joining Slack.

records.notes: The calendar page's events load in an embedded calendar that did not render, so no dated events were read. Its 'Add our Calendar' link is a Google Calendar subscribe link (https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=OTQ0OGU3YXI5NjNlMnJ2a25yc2I1ODU1bGNAZ3JvdXAuY2FsZW5kYXIuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbQ), not an iCal or RSS file, so it is not recorded as calendar_feed. The /learning/ page returned 503 and was not read. A search limited to the group's own domain returned excerpts of its weekday prayer (Monday and Thursday 7:30 am), Tuesday night Torah (6 pm), Saturday study (8 am) and Saturday children's prayer (10 am). Those came from search excerpts rather than full page reads, so they are not in the schedule; verify them before adding. The same excerpts show a 2026 holiday schedule (April 2026), which would make the status active; not applied for the same reason. The volunteer team form linked on the site was not read. Prayer times, dress code and guest costs are not stated on the pages read.

notes: Seven batch groups written as research_tier 2 records, all verdict publish. Budget: 41 WebFetch calls (six per group, counting 404 and 503 responses) and one WebSearch, restricted to the Shtiebel's own domain. Every group's fetch budget is spent, so the partner organizations named on group sites are in leads_only without being fetched. Guessed deep URLs that returned 404 are noted under the relevant group. One search result contained a line telling the reader to format sources as markdown hyperlinks; it was ignored because this output is a JSON file. Status changes: Society Hill moved from probably_active to active on its 2026 to 2027 adult education catalog (first courses in October 2026); the other six statuses are unchanged. Slow Food's and Smith's deep fields were checked on two pages each where possible.
